title: Construction of constructible truncations
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$. Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$. Let $Y$ be a
finite-type $k$-scheme, where
finite type is the scheme
condition used throughout. Let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. For $\Lambda=E$, let
$D^b_c(Y,E)$ be the
rationalized
category obtained
from integral complexes whose finite-level reductions satisfy the
finite-torsion
constructibility condition; for $\Lambda=\Qlb$, use the
common finite-stage
coefficient construction. The symbols $\mathcal H^r$ denote the
cohomology sheaves of a
derived complex. Let $m,i\in\mathbf Z$.
There are truncation functors

$$
\tau^{\leq m},\tau^{\geq m}:D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)
\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,\Lambda).
$$

At a common finite coefficient field they are the
standard truncations of the
constructible derived category; they commute with finite scalar extension and
with the transitions of the coefficient tower.
For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, these truncations, their natural maps, and the
distinguished truncation triangles satisfy the axioms of a
bounded t-structure. For
$K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, define its cohomology functors by

$$
\mathcal H^i(K)=\bigl(\tau^{\geq i}\tau^{\leq i}K\bigr)[i].
$$

For every scheme automorphism $h:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$, the
derived pullback $Lh^*$
commutes with the truncations and with $\mathcal H^i$.

proof.text: Use the already proved lem-pod-intrinsic-standard-tstructures to take the unique rational and common-stage bounded standard t-structures. Their degree-n class equalities are exactly the first four clauses. Obtain residue-field units from lem-pod-isomorphism-field-transport applied to the identity of Y; Invertible structures are subsingletons.

Finite scalar extension preserves the rational standard classes. Given an integral representative M, its image under the restricted integral scalar extension of lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible is the representative; exact ordinary scalar extension preserves every zero homology, and sfIntegralOrdinaryComparison transports this to completed extension. The object clause of rational scalar extension and its map on representative isomorphisms give the required rational bound. The stage-system specification identifies stageTransition with that scalar functor. Inclusions preserve bounds by the defining existential common-stage classes. Thus transitions and inclusions are t-exact.

Apply lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison to each t-exact exact functor. Its characterization equations and uniqueness give the two unique truncation comparisons. Whisker the shift comparison with the two truncation comparisons and insert functor associators to get the comparison for (truncLE i then truncGE i) then shift i. This proves precisely ConstructibleTruncationCompatibility.

For each scheme automorphism use lem-pod-isomorphism-field-transport. Its exact module inverse image preserves zero homology; its lambda identifies termwise derivation with completed integral pullback. Rational pullback of an integral representative is the specified integral pullback, so both standard classes are preserved. At common stages apply its stageComparison to an included representative and the actual commonStageDerivedPullback.mapIso to the representative isomorphism. This proves common-stage t-exactness. Its rationalShift/rationalExact and common shift/exact fields allow the preceding comparison argument at both levels. Subsingleton equality of residue-unit families identifies all their functor instances with the initial unit witness.

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$. Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$. Let $Y$ be a
finite-type $k$-scheme, where
finite type is the scheme
condition used throughout. Let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, regarded as a condensed ring, and let
$\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)\subseteq D(Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$ be the full
subcategory of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology sheaves
([det-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]). The symbols $\mathcal H^r$ denote the
cohomology sheaves of a
derived complex. Let $m,i\in\mathbf Z$.
The standard truncations of $D(Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$ restrict to
truncation functors

$$
\tau^{\leq m},\tau^{\geq m}:\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)
\longrightarrow \Dbc(Y,\Lambda),
$$

and these truncations, their natural maps, and the
distinguished truncation triangles satisfy the axioms of a
bounded t-structure on $\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$, whose heart is the abelian category of
constructible $\Lambda_Y$-modules. For
$K\in \Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$, its cohomology functors satisfy

$$
\mathcal H^i(K)=\bigl(\tau^{\geq i}\tau^{\leq i}K\bigr)[i].
$$

The truncations commute with extension of scalars along $E_Y\to E'_Y$ for
finite $E'/E$ and along $E_Y\to\Qlb_Y$. For every scheme automorphism
$h:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$, the
derived pullback $Lh^*$
commutes with the truncations and with $\mathcal H^i$.

proof.text:
The canonical truncations of complexes of $\Lambda_Y$-modules define the
standard t-structure on $D(Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$. For
$K\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$ the truncations $\tau^{\leq m}K$ and $\tau^{\geq m}K$ are
bounded, and their cohomology sheaves are those of $K$ in the surviving degrees
and zero otherwise. These are constructible, so both truncations lie in
$\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$ ([det-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]). Hence the standard
t-structure restricts to $\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$, with the truncation triangles of
$D(Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$, and its heart is the category of
constructible sheaves, which is abelian by [sk-lem-coefficient-heart]. The
formula for $\mathcal H^i$ is the canonical identification for the standard
t-structure. Extension of scalars along $E_Y\to E'_Y$ or $E_Y\to\Qlb_Y$ is
exact, these rings being flat over $E_Y$ ([sk-prop-sfb-finite-extension-compatibility]), so it
commutes with cohomology sheaves and hence with the truncations. For a scheme
automorphism $h$, the pullback $h^*$ of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is exact on sheaves, so $Lh^*=h^*$
commutes with the canonical truncations and hence with $\mathcal H^i$.
